attack: C8 — an artifact-level successor the maintainer does not control
fixture: adversarial-1.1.0 (paired against miri-1.1.0, which does not carry it)
clause: clause 2 — replacement is not a well-formed successor
note: The highest-severity documented redirect: a compromised release migrating its dependents onto an attacker-held successor. A consumer that auto-migrates performs the supply-chain attack itself.

must_not_report_on.why: The conforming arm does not carry this attack. A linter reporting the same check on both arms has detected nothing — it reports unconditionally, and would score identically against a fixture with no attacks at all.

linter_assertion.evidence: support.status is deprecated and support.replacement is pkg:pypi/attacker-greetctl@9.0.0 — a different PEP 503 normalized distribution name from identity.purl's greetctl.

paired_control.why: greetctl.py is byte-identical across all four arms — the builder fails if the digests diverge — so the arms differ only in the two JSON files beside it. A difference in what a linter reports is therefore attributable to metadata, not code. Neither arm decides the case alone: the attack arm catches a linter that reports nothing, the control arm catches one that reports everything.

why_this_case_was_missing: PyPI has no namespace, so the name is the only discriminator — and `greetctl` is a SUBSTRING of `attacker-greetctl`. A substring test reports no redirect. This trap caught a first draft of this fixture's own validator, and it is the same correction MIRI-CONSUMER-032 needed.
